podcast.body: Brian Wilson conceived this project as an attempt to record the "best album in history," aiming to define the decade and expand music to new levels before The Beatles could. Following the success of Pet Sounds and "Good Vibrations," The Beach Boys reached an agreement with Capital Records for a release on January 15, 1967. However, after 10 months of intense work, the band was forced to cancel the album in May 1967, due to Brian Wilson's deep depressions, mental disorders, growing tensions within the band, and his increasing paranoia. Over 150 hours of recordings were archived. "Esta es la historia de Smile, el disco perdido que pudo cambiar la historia de la música."

podcast.body: In 2011, an official edition of Smile was finally released, compiling the recordings made by the band during those 10 months of intense work in the 1960s. This release allowed the public to experience the original studio work from the legendary unreleased album. "Esto ha permitido que en 2011, se lanzara al fin un edición oficial de Smiley con las grabaciones que hizo la banda durante esos 10 meses de los años 60."
